euronews.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Primetime' - Robert Pattinson needs to catch his predator (and ratings)

euronews.title: Explosion near Acropolis collapses building in Athens’ Plaka, injuring two
euronews.description: A powerful explosion in Athens’ historic Plaka district brought down a two-storey building near the Acropolis on Friday 25 September 2026, injuring at least two people. The cause remains under investigation, although a gas leak is suspected.

euronews.title: Euronews explains: What would a US diesel export ban mean to European countries?
euronews.description: The EU has deepened energy ties with the US while seeking to reduce its exposure to geopolitical shocks. Yet US plans to limit diesel exports expose how quickly commercial dependence can become a strategic vulnerability.

euronews.title: Turkish forces to withdraw from strategic military base in northern Iraq
euronews.description: Turkey will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zilkan camp, where it has had troops since 2015, to the Iraqi government.

euronews.title: Europe's top leagues add to pressure on Infantino by calling for FIFA reform
euronews.description: It is the latest rift between football leagues and Infantino, whose biggest projects have been seen as attacks on domestic football and were successfully resisted by a backlash from European officials.

euronews.title: The business of peace: US investment push takes the TRIPP corridor from diplomacy to trade
euronews.description: Washington grants millions to the so-called Trans-Caspian Enterprise Fund to act as a catalyst for private investment in the South Caucasus and Central Asia.

euronews.description: Four artists have been shortlisted for this year’s Turner Prize, with their work now on display at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art in northern England.

euronews.title: Kazakhstan wants crypto miners to use power generated by excess oil field gas
euronews.description: Kazakhstan is allowing crypto miners to use excess associated gas from oil fields to generate their own electricity, in a bid to reduce gas flaring and increase oil output while attracting miners back to the country.

rfi.title: Live: Worshippers and clergy wait for the Pope on the streets of Paris
rfi.description: Crowds on Friday cheered Pope Leo XIV as he began a popemobile tour in the heart of Paris, waving to well-wishers on his way to the Notre Dame Cathedral.

rfi.title: Pope Leo's visit to Paris migrant centre sends message ahead of French election
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV will on Saturday visit Maison Bakhita, a church-run centre for migrants and other marginalised groups in the north of Paris, bearing a message of charity and acceptance. Part of his four-day state tour of France, the visit comes just months before a presidential election set to be dominated by anti-immigration rhetoric.

rfi.title: EDF faces legal action over France’s continuing nuclear ties with Russia
rfi.description: France’s continuing reliance on Russia for part of its nuclear fuel cycle is facing a new legal challenge, with Greenpeace seeking to force French state electricity company EDF to address the environmental, health and human rights implications of its dealings with Russian state nuclear group Rosatom.

rfi.title: Senegal's President Faye: Macky Sall best candidate 'to fight for Africa' at UN
rfi.description: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has thrown his weight behind his predecessor and former political rival Macky Sall to become the next United Nations secretary-general. No one is better placed to fight for Africa's place at the table, he told RFI and France 24.

rfi.title: France to send military to protect Saudi Arabia on Red Sea oil route
rfi.description: France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which is key for energy transport, French President Emmanuel Macron has said in a TV interview. He also denied a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the US Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments of possible Russian drone attacks from the Mediterranean.

rfi.title: Egypt, Senegal, Morocco and Nigeria start quest for AFCON 2027
rfi.description: Seven-time champions Egypt and heavyweight outfits Nigeria, Morocco and Senegal begin their qualifying campaigns on Friday for next year's Africa Cup of Nations.

rfi.title: Ethiopia fighting spreads beyond Tigray as internet disrupted
rfi.description: Ethiopian forces battled overnight to repel an assault by Tigray rebels in the Afar region, a humanitarian source said Friday, with reports of an internet blackout in the north of the country.

rfi.title: Zidane stresses role as second fiddle to France players ahead of Turkey clash
rfi.description: France's new head coach Zinedine Zidane has played down his own star status and put the focus firmly on his players as they prepare for his first match in charge against Turkey in Izmit on Friday night.

rfi.title: French authorities investigate racist abuse of judo star Teddy Riner
rfi.description: Authorities are investigating online racial abuse and harassment targeting French judo star Teddy Riner, after he expressed his concern over the rise of the far right in the country.

rfi.title: Nigeria faces world’s highest heat death toll as El Nino bears down on Sahel
rfi.description: Extreme heat generated by this year's El Nino is projected to cause up to 67,000 additional deaths across the Sahel over the next six months, with Nigeria facing the highest death toll of any country in the world.

rfi.title: Côte d'Ivoire outfox Ghana on Renard's return in Afcon 2027 qualifier
rfi.description: Hervé Renard launched his second spell as Côte d’Ivoire head coach with a 2-0 victory over Ghana in the first qualifying game for next year's Africa Cup of Nations in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

rfi.title: Concern grows over Algeria's plans to end moratorium on death penalty
rfi.description: Algeria is moving towards ending its 33-year moratorium on executions, with proposed changes to the penal code now before the country's parliament. The new measures would provide for the death penalty for those convicted of abuses against children and arson. Human rights organisations have signed a petition against the move, saying it will not act as a deterrent.

rfi.title: French-language author Orélien denies using AI to write award-winning book
rfi.description: Canadian-Haitian writer Thélyson Orélien this week denied using artificial intelligence to write parts of his book "It Was Either That or Die" – which has won several French literary awards – after being targeted by accusations from an anonymous online account.

rfi.title: Podcast: Pope in secular France, vultures and farmers, first divorce law
rfi.description: With its strong commitment to secularism, France is not an obvious place for Pope Leo XIV to stage an appearance, but his visit is drawing interest from Catholics and non-Catholics alike. After nearly disappearing from France, vultures are making a comeback, but their return has created new tensions with farmers. And France's revolutionary first divorce law from 1792.

rfi.title: Trump hosts China's Xi for high-stakes summit ahead of US midterm elections
rfi.description: US President Donald Trump has welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington for a high-stakes state visit, rolling out the red carpet as the two leaders seek to preserve a fragile truce while confronting tensions over trade, Taiwan and Iran. With US midterm elections approaching and Republicans at risk of losing control of Congress, Trump also has a domestic political stake in making the summit a success.

rfi.title: Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers begin with 2025 champions still undecided
rfi.description: Qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations get underway on Thursday, with a heavyweight clash between Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire the pick of the bunch. Meanwhile, top sports lawyers are preparing to thrash out whether Senegal or Morocco won the 2025 edition of the tournament.

rfi.title: Morocco’s PAM comes first in election marked by record-low voter turnout
rfi.description: Morocco's centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), which is part of the kingdom's ruling coalition, came out ahead in Wednesday's parliamentary election after winning 97 out of 395 seats, according to provisional results.

rfi.title: The global machinery built to carry out Trump’s mass deportation drive
rfi.description: More than 25,000 people have been deported by the United States to countries other than their own since Donald Trump returned to power. As part of The Deportation Project, coordinated by Forbidden Stories – a Paris-based journalism network that pursues the work of reporters who have been threatened, jailed or killed – RFI is publishing investigations into how this policy operates, with their findings exposing a global system backed by hundreds of millions of dollars.

lemonde.description: Les Verts reprochent au sénateur de Paris son soutien officiel au député européen pour 2027, et sa participation annoncée à un débat, prévu le 10 octobre, sous les couleurs de Place publique, face aux Ecologistes.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les attaques russes sur Kiev ont tué au moins cinq personnes depuis le début de la journée, selon le maire de la ville

lemonde.description: Une exposition présentée au Petit Trianon plonge le visiteur dans l’ambiance de ce long-métrage, devenu culte, qui bousculait l’image de la reine, incarnée par Kirsten Dunst.

lemonde.title: Près de 1 000 épargnants coincés dans la liquidation d’une SCPI
lemonde.description: Etranglé par une collecte nulle et un endettement important, le fonds Essentialis a fait voter sa dissolution par ses associés lors d’une assemblée générale extraordinaire. Ils doivent maintenant attendre que les gérants vendent tous leurs actifs immobiliers pour espérer revoir une partie seulement de leur argent, car des pertes sont à prévoir.

france24fr.title: Guerre hybride : le spectre de la menace russe plane sur la Méditerranée
france24fr.description: La CIA aurait averti plusieurs pays que la Russie se préparerait à lancer des opérations hybrides depuis la mer Méditerranée. Le risque est-il réel ou s'agit-il d'une opération de guerre informationnelle ?

france24fr.title: Léon XIV en France : la papamobile déambule vers Notre-Dame de Paris
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV a débuté vendredi 25 septembre dans l'après-midi une déambulation en papamobile au coeur de Paris en direction de la cathédrale Notre-Dame, saluant de la main une foule en liesse. Les autorités attendaient 250 000 personnes le long d'un parcours de 2,5 kilomètres entre Montparnasse et la place Saint-Michel, située à deux pas de Notre-Dame. Les précisions de Johan Bodin, journaliste correspondant à France 24.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV en France : ambiance sur le parcours de la papamobile
france24fr.description: Dans les rues de Paris, les fidèles et curieux se sont réunis dans l'après-midi du 25 septembre, un peu partout sur le parcours de la papamobile que tracera le pape Léon XIV en direction de la cathédrale Notre-Dame.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : Léon XIV arrive à Notre-Dame-de-Paris, première visite papale depuis sa réouverture
Visite de Léon XIV en France : le pape quitte l'UNESCO en papamobile
france24fr.description: Après son discours à l'UNESCO, vendredi 25 septembre, le pape Léon XIV se dirige vers la cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris dans la fameuse papamobile sur 2.5 kilomètres pour aller à la rencontre des fidèles qui l'attende.

france24fr.title: REPLAY - Léon XIV à l'UNESCO : "les dirigeants mondiaux bafouent" l'État de droit
france24fr.description: Le souverain pontife a pris la parole vendredi 25 septembre à l'UNESCO, en français et en anglais en appuyant sur la situation géopolitique : "au lieu de respecter la loi, ceux qui détiennent le pouvoir l’invoquent lorsqu’elle sert leurs intérêts et la bafouent lorsqu’elle les entrave, traitant même la justice elle-même comme s’il s’agissait d’une marchandise que l’on peut acheter et vendre", a affirmé le souverain pontife.

france24fr.title: La Belgique renoue avec le Rwanda et conserve son influence en Afrique centrale
france24fr.description: La Belgique et le Rwanda ont annoncé, en marge de l'Assemblée générale des Nations Unies à New-York, le rétablissement de leurs relations diplomatiques. Ces dernières avaient été rompues il y a un an et demi après des sanctions de l'Union européenne contre des chefs militaires rwandais, dans le cadre du conflit entre la République démocratique du Congo et l'AFC/M23 soutenu par le Rwanda.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV en France : une arrivée du ovationnée à l'UNESCO
france24fr.description: Le directeur général de l'UNESCO Khaled El-Enany est arrivé, dans l'après-midi du vendredi 25 septembre, accompagné de Léon XIV, acclamé, sur la scène. Le pape fera son discours à la suite du directeur de l'UNESCO, puis prendra son premier bain de foule sur 2,5 km en papamobile dans le centre de Paris, où le public commençait à se rassembler.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : "combats intenses" entre les rebelles du Tigré et les forces fédérales
france24fr.description: D'intenses combats ont opposé dans la nuit de jeudi 24 septembre, les forces fédérales éthiopiennes à des troupes des autorités rebelles du Tigré dans la ville d'Abala, dans l'État régional voisin de l'Afar. Les forces fédérales "ont empêché les rebelles d'entrer dans la ville" située au sein de massifs marquant la frontière avec l'est du Tigré.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV en France : une venue du pape apostolique et non politique ?
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV a entamé vendredi 25 septembre à Paris une visite apostolique de quatre jours en France, "terre de riches racines chrétiennes" où il a d'emblée plaidé en faveur de la paix dans un discours à l'Élysée aux côtés d'Emmanuel Macron, questionnant l'influence que peut avoir le chef de l'Église catholique sur les décisions politiques. Les précisions de Constance Colonna Cesaria, journaliste spécialiste de la papauté.

france24fr.title: Violences sexistes et sexuelles : la loi intégrale peut-elle changer la donne en France ?
france24fr.description: La proposition de "loi intégrale" a été votée en commission parlementaire et les débats sur le texte vont commencer le 1er octobre dans l’hémicycle de l’Assemblée nationale. Conçue pour lutter "à 360 degrés" contre ce fléau qui fait régulièrement les gros titres de la presse, elle se veut complète : prévention, formation et réparation. france24fr.title: Léon XIV à Parix : 2,5 kilomètres de déambulation sous haute sécurité
france24fr.description: Après sa venue à l'Élysée en fin de matinée, vendredi 25 septembre, le pape Léon XIV s'apprête à faire un discours à l'UNESCO avant de déambuler sur environ 2,5 kilomètres vers la place Saint-Michel. Les explications de Johan Bodin, journaliste à France 24.

france24fr.title: Arabie saoudite - France : l'envoi de "moyens militaires" pour "protéger" un site clé
france24fr.description: L'Arabie saoudite a annoncé jeudi 24 septembre, avoir intercepté une attaque de missiles tirés du Yémen voisin par les Houthis pro-iraniens, sur fond d'intensification des hostilités entre les deux parties. Les défenses aériennes ont abattu six missiles visant les régions de Taïf et de Yanbu, sur la mer Rouge. Emmanuel Macron a déclaré y envoyer des "moyens militaires" pour "protéger" ces sites énergétiques clés.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV bientôt au Stade de France : la ferveur des jeunes croyants monte à Saint-Denis
france24fr.description: À quelques heures de la veillée de prière au Stade de France, la ferveur monte, l'impatience est là. De jeunes chrétiens se sont déjà rassemblé à Bondy, une commune de Saint-Denis, pour partager leur enthousiasme.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : suivez le discours du pape Léon XIV à l'Unesco
Ethiopie : les combats s’intensifient entre les forces fédérales et des groupes armés
france24fr.description: En Éthiopie, les combats entre les forces fédérales et des groupes armés font rage dans les États régionaux voisins de l'Amhara et de l'Afar. Les autorités rebelles du Tigré ont déclaré la guerre totale contre le gouvernement éthiopien. Au total, 272 rebelles ont été tués dans le nord du pays, selon l'armée fédérale.

france24fr.title: Léon XIV : discours du pape au palais de l'Élysée
france24fr.description: Dans les premiers mots de son allocution, le souverain pontife fait l'éloge du rayonnement historique du pays : "Depuis des siècles, la France brille comme un phare culturel, artistique et spirituel. Forte de ses écoles-cathédrales, de ses universités, de ses académies, la France a contribué à forger l'intelligence des populations, bien au-delà de ses frontières." france24fr.title: RD Congo : les populations de Bukavu inquiètes après un nouvel incendie meurtrier
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 Nouvel incendie meurtrier à Bukavu, dans l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo. Le sinistre a frappé le quartier de Nyalukemba, quelques jours après un autre incendie qui avait fait 27 morts. Les habitants réclament une enquête sur ces feux à répétition.

nzz.description: Das Prestigeprojekt hätte ein gesichtsloses Uferstück in eine spektakuläre Promenade über dem Zürichsee verwandeln sollen. Daraus wird nun nichts.

nzz.title: Breel Embolo fehlt der Schweiz in der Nations League
nzz.description: Der SFV verzichtet für den laufenden Zusammenzug auf den Stürmer. Zuvor war bekannt geworden, dass Embolo wegen gefälschter Covid-Testzertifikate einen Strafbefehl akzeptiert hat.

nzz.title: Angriffe auf Internetanbieter: Russland will die Ukraine vom Netz nehmen
nzz.description: Die russischen Streitkräfte versuchen, die ukrainische Kommunikationsinfrastruktur zu zerstören. In Polen kommt es zu einem ungeklärten Brand an einer Starlink-Bodenstation. Auch sie hat für die Ukraine militärische Bedeutung.

nzz.title: Zurich Film Festival: Das sind die besten Bilder zum Auftakt
nzz.description: Zürich steht im Zeichen des Filmfestivals: Weltstars, Politiker und bekannte Persönlichkeiten aus dem Internet liefen über den grünen Teppich.

nzz.title: Zu hohe Rindfleischpreise, veraltete Lokale und kaum Poulet: McDonald’s-Restaurants brauchen Milliardenhilfe
nzz.description: Mit über 46 000 Filialen ist McDonald’s der weltgrösste Betreiber von Fast-Food-Restaurants. Doch viele Konsumenten sparen beim Auswärtsessen. Der Aktienkurs des US-Riesen ist deutlich gefallen.

nzz.title: VIDEO - «Wir müssen uns fragen, wie oft wir in Zukunft noch Briefe zustellen», sagt der Post-CEO Pascal Grieder
nzz.description: In der neuen Folge «NZZ Weekend» spricht der Post-CEO Pascal Grieder übers Briefeschreiben und Preiserhöhungen. Auch die Schweizoffensive der britischen Konkurrentin Revolut ist Thema. Die ganze Folge hören Sie hier.

nzz.description: Peter A. Fischer, Georg Häsler und Matthias Kamp diskutieren über die Zukunft der Beziehungen zwischen China und Amerika.

nzz.description: lia. /(dpa) Zwischen den deutschen Chemiekonzernen BASF und Evonik finden offenbar wieder Gespräche über eine mögliche Übernahme statt. Das berichten am Freitag (25. 9.) unter anderem die «Financial Times» (FT) und das «Handelsblatt».

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - «Erschreckendes Ausmass an Gewalt»: Acht Jugendliche und junge Erwachsene verhaftet – Strafverfahren wegen versuchter Tötung eröffnet

nzz.title: Der FC Basel hat einen neuen Trainer gefunden
nzz.description: Der 58-jährige serbisch-spanische Doppelbürger Slavisa Jokanovic wird Nachfolger von Stephan Lichtsteiner.

nzz.title: Jetzt muss der Zürcher Stadtrat sparen: Er reduziert die Liegenschaftskäufe drastisch – und verzichtet auf den Bau der Marina Tiefenbrunnen
nzz.description: Die Aussicht auf einen Schuldenberg von 16 Milliarden Franken bis 2030 zwingt die Exekutive zum Handeln. Nun droht ein Streit mit dem Stadtparlament.

nzz.title: Iran will in sieben Tagen die Strasse von Hormuz öffnen – falls die USA Konzessionen machen
nzz.description: Irans Anführer wollen den Krieg offenbar beendet sehen und machen zum ersten Mal seit Wochen ein diplomatisches Angebot. Doch die iranischen Forderungen bleiben bestehen – in Teheran gibt es wenig Spielraum für Kompromisse.

observador.title: Emídio Guerreiro preside a comissão de inquérito aos exames
observador.description: Emídio Guerreiro (PSD) presidirá ao inquérito proposto pelo BE sobre a classificação digital dos exames de 2025 e 2026. Investigação tem prazo de 90 dias.

observador.title: Portugal à espera de saber o rumo da tempestade. Pode hav...
observador.description: Que vai chover, vai, já domingo. Até lá, a diferença entre o dia e a noite pode ser de 20ºC. Depois, depende do rumo da tempestade, mas as trovoadas podem ficar toda a semana. E os 30ºC não voltam.

observador.title: 16h. PR promulga três diplomas do Governo
observador.description: Um dos diplomas está relacionado com as ajudas para fazer face ao aumento do preço dos combustíveis. Ainda, PGR afasta mau ambiente entre Ministério Público e Polícia Judiciária.

observador.title: Saída de presidente da AIMA foi decidida por Leitão Amaro
observador.description: Decisão foi tomada no início do verão pelo Ministério da Presidência e depois acordada com o próprio. Caso acabou revelado numa nota do Parlamento. Transição para AdC já teve luz verde.

observador.title: 200 advogados contra multas por manobras dilatórias
observador.description: Uma carta aberta pede à Assembleia da República que elimine ou reformule o artigo que penaliza atos vistos como dilatórios, alertando para riscos à defesa e às garantias fundamentais.

observador.title: Novo filme de Brady Corbet com filmagens em Almada
observador.description: "The Origin of the World" é o próximo filme do realizador de "O Brutalista". Parte da rodagem aconteceu discretamente este mês, incluindo cenas gravadas na Ponte 25 de Abril.

observador.title: Estremoz. Quatro mortos em lar onde foi detetada Gripe A
observador.description: O surto foi detetado domingo no Lar da Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Veiros. As vítimas mortais tinham entre 89 e 95 anos. Visitas estão suspensas e instalações desinfetadas.

observador.title: Tiago Vilhena: "Se não fosse a música estava muito mal"
observador.description: Após quatro anos, Tiago Vilhena regressa com "Salatrano", um álbum nascido de um sonho que junta indie rock e kizomba para celebrar a amizade.

observador.title: Procurador-Geral da República nega "mau ambiente" com PJ
observador.description: Amadeu Guerra realçou que "não há ambiente pesado" entre as duas instituições e sublinhou que o "valor" da PJ deve ser respeitado, após buscas por parte do Ministério Público.

observador.title: Das ondas ao green
observador.description: No Tee, recebemos o surfista Kikas e o golfista Tomás Bessa, que conversam sobre a consistência, a exigência mental e a emoção de representar Portugal nos Jogos Olímpicos.

observador.title: 15h. PGR afasta mau ambiente entre MP e PJ após buscas
observador.description: Inquérito quer apurar se atual diretor da PJ participou em escuta ilegal no caso Football Leaks. Ainda, ministro da Educação acusa FENPROF de tudo ter feito para que avaliação dos exames corresse mal.

observador.title: Governo aprova acordo de empréstimo com a CE
observador.description: Conselho de Ministros deu luz verde ao acordo com Bruxelas que financia fragatas, blindados, satélites e drones. Acordo operacional previsto para outubro.

observador.title: Ministro: Fenprof fez tudo para que correção corresse mal
observador.description: Fernando Alexandre disse que este Governo pagou três milhões de euros a mais de 11 mil professores classificadores, dos quais, cerca de 10 mil receberam em agosto, "como tinha prometido".

observador.title: Aprovada iniciativa para reduzir sobrecustos da insulardade
observador.description: Pela segunda vez em dois dias, o Parlamento rejeitou a maioria das iniciativas sobre o custo de vida. Só uma recomendação do JPP para as regiões autónomas passou.

observador.title: Da reunião "secreta" com Belém ao código "idiota" de Costa
observador.description: "Contas Certas", livro de Mário Centeno lançado esta sexta-feira, revela episódios da sua entrada na política, tensões com António Costa e uma ambição que parece ir para lá das finanças públicas.

observador.title: 14h. Leão XIV diz que há "risco de cair na ilusão" sobre IA
observador.description: Chefe da Igreja Católica deixa ainda recado a Donald Trump sobre proibição dos meios de comunicação na Casa Branca. Ainda, protesto do setor das terraplanagens termina com "objetivos cumpridos".

observador.title: Benjamin Netanyahu rejeita genocídio em Gaza
observador.description: Primeiro-ministro israelita acusa delegados da ONU de serem “cobardes morais” ao abandonarem a Assembleia. Ainda, Irão diz-se disponível para negociar a paz.

observador.title: João Félix foi o grande destaque no triunfo de Portugal
observador.description: Portugal bateu Gales por 1-0 na estreia de Jorge Jesus. João Félix e Ruben Dias sobressaíram, enquanto Cristiano Ronaldo e Bruno Fernandes sentiram adaptações no novo modelo tático.

spiegel.title: Premier League: Manchester City soll in 114 Fällen gegen Finanzregeln verstoßen haben
spiegel.description: Seit Jahren wird untersucht, ob ManCity Finanzregularien der Premier League gebrochen hat. Der Club sei nun in einem »Großteil« der Anklagepunkte für schuldig befunden worden, berichten britische Medien.

spiegel.title: Gremlins 3: Kein Sonnenlicht, kein Wasser, niemals nach Mitternacht füttern, nicht vor 2028 im Kino gucken
spiegel.description: Die gute Nachricht: Es gibt einen allerersten, brandneuen Teaser für den dritten Teil des Horror-Klassikers »Gremlins«. Die schlechte: Der Kinostart verschiebt sich.

spiegel.title: Spanien: Frau und Tochter leben zwei Jahre mit Leiche im Haus nahe Barcelona
spiegel.description: In der Nähe von Barcelona melden Anwohner den Behörden ein Müllproblem an einem Haus in ihrer Nachbarschaft. Die Polizei rückt an – und macht eine grausige Entdeckung.

spiegel.title: Sandra Hüller fand ihren Weg ins Schauspiel über ein Jobcenter
spiegel.description: Mit dem Film »Astronaut« machte sich Sandra Hüller in Hollywood einen Namen. Für den neuen Streifen »Digger« drehte sie mit Tom Cruise. In »Late Night« mit Seth Meyers hat sie über ihre Anfänge berichtet.

spiegel.title: Köln: WDR baut Stellen ab und streicht 76 Angebote
spiegel.description: Fernsehsendungen, Podcasts, Social-Media-Angebote: Der WDR stellt nach eigenen Angaben bis Ende 2027 Dutzende Formate ein. Neue Angebote sollen entwickelt werden, jedoch mit immer weniger Personal.

spiegel.title: Rückruf bei VW, Verkehrsminister Bilger über die Deutsche Bahn, Treffen Trump und Xi Jinping
spiegel.description: Volkswagen ruft Millionen Autos zurück. Der Verkehrsminister will aufräumen. Und Trump macht sich vor Xi Jinping lächerlich. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Atomuhr auf Lutetium-Basis: Neuer Rekord! Das ist die genaueste Uhr der Welt
spiegel.description: 55 Milliarden Jahre – so lange dauert es, bis eine neue, in Singapur entwickelte Atomuhr nicht mehr die korrekte Zeit anzeigen würde. Wie genau sie funktioniert und was die Uhr so besonders macht.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, Techbosse: Wer beim Dinner neben den Präsidenten saß
spiegel.description: Zum Staatsbesuch des chinesischen Präsidenten hat Donald Trump das Who’s who der amerikanischen Wirtschaft eingeladen. Die Sitzordnung lässt darauf schließen, wer dem Mann im Weißen Haus derzeit besonders nah ist.

spiegel.title: Roman wegen KI-Verdachts aus Liste für französischen Literaturpreis gestrichen
spiegel.description: Der Roman von Thélyson Orélien soll »sehr weitgehend das Produkt künstlicher Intelligenz« sein. Jetzt hat der Goncourt-Preis ihn von der Liste geworfen.

spiegel.title: Evonik: Übernahmegespräche mit BASF treiben Evonik-Kurs in die Höhe
spiegel.description: Der Chemieriese BASF ​hat laut einem Bericht der »Financial Times« den Konkurrenten ‌Evonik im Visier. Deren Aktie zieht an, bestätigen will man das Interesse aber nur als »unverbindliche Anfrage«.

spiegel.title: Formel-1-Qualifying in Baku: WM-Spitzenreiter Kimi Antonelli nach Crash nur 16.
spiegel.description: Kimi Antonelli startet von weit hinten beim Großen Preis von Aserbaidschan, der WM-Führende touchierte im Qualifying früh die Wand. Auch Max Verstappen fuhr ein enttäuschendes Ergebnis ein.

spiegel.title: VW: Rückruf von Golf, Tiguan, Touran, Audi Q3 und Skoda
spiegel.description: Allein in Deutschland muss der VW-Konzern 900.000 Pkw zurückrufen, inklusive Audi und Škoda. Es geht um eine profane Schraube, die rosten könnte, mit ernsten Folgen. So finden Sie heraus, ob Ihr Auto betroffen ist.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Was will Emmanuel Macron mit Soldaten in Saudi-Arabien?
spiegel.description: Der Präsident will mit französischen Soldaten einen Ölhafen in Saudi-Arabien schützen – und bringt damit die Populisten Le Pen und Mélenchon gegen sich auf, die um seine Nachfolge rangeln.

spiegel.title: WhatsApp: Kriminelle kapern Konten über fingierte Abstimmungsanfragen
spiegel.description: Mit fingierten Abstimmungen verschaffen sich Betrüger Zugriff auf WhatsApp-Accounts. Wie die Masche funktioniert, warum sie so gefährlich ist und wie Sie sich schützen.

spiegel.title: Arbeitsmarkt: Flexible Personalplanung nimmt zu, Beschäftigte tragen die Last
spiegel.description: Befristungen, Arbeitszeitkonten, Überstunden: Die deutsche Wirtschaft setzt zunehmend auf flexible Personalplanung. Beschäftigte zahlen den Preis.

spiegel.title: »Grüffelo«: Illustrator Axel Scheffler will seinen Grüffelo nicht auf dem Oktoberfest sehen

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

proj-syn.title: The Great AI Gamble
proj-syn.description: As the two world leaders in AI development and adoption, the United States and China are each operating under assumptions that justify ever-faster progress, regardless of the risks. The current thinking is not unlike the rationale once given for Stalinist brutality in the name of rapid modernization.

proj-syn.title: The Un-Ordered UN Order
proj-syn.description: As European leaders hobnob with their counterparts at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, they must think carefully about how to navigate a fast-changing multilateral landscape. The old world belonged to rule-makers and institution-builders, but the current one favors those who can improvise.

proj-syn.title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
proj-syn.description: As people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news, the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable. UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.

proj-syn.title: How to Stop the AI-pocalypse
proj-syn.description: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity, yet efforts to slow its development may fail as companies and countries race to stay ahead. Preventing such a future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth that could put unprecedented power in the hands of a tiny elite.

proj-syn.title: What Killed Liberalism?
proj-syn.description: There is no shortage of people and ideas to blame for liberalism’s decline, but searching for a single culprit is probably futile. Two new books by Gordon Brown and Daron Acemoglu take up the harder question of how to rebuild the institutions that once gave people a sense of community and power over their lives.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the German Question
proj-syn.description: Until this month, a far-right, openly ethnonationalist party had never come so close to winning an absolute majority in an election in the Federal Republic of Germany. Now that it has, and with similarly pro-Russian forces on the rise in France, all Europeans must prepare for the worst.

proj-syn.title: UN Peacekeeping in Crisis
proj-syn.description: With the world facing the largest number of armed conflicts since 1946, the Trump administration’s continuing assault on the United Nations has prevented the organization from fulfilling its peacekeeping duties. A recent report by UN Secretary-General António Guterres shows how the organization has few, if any, levers to fight back.

proj-syn.title: Lies, Election Lies, and Trump’s Statisticians
proj-syn.description: An obviously amateurish brief published by the US Census Bureau should raise alarms for all businesses, investors, and others who rely on official government statistics. By recklessly undermining trust in what should be an apolitical public service, Donald Trump is jeopardizing a critical pillar of American prosperity.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the IMF to Latin America
proj-syn.description: Over the past decade, many Latin American and Caribbean countries internalized IMF-style policy discipline without having active IMF programs, producing fragile stagnation—and an opening for the Fund to swoop back in. This could end up helping the United States reassert its dominance over the region.

proj-syn.title: The AI Plot Thickens
proj-syn.description: When it comes to AI, it is difficult to know what to believe. Are the CEOs, researchers, and investors who tout the technology’s seemingly unlimited capabilities more credible, because they work directly with it, or less credible, because they stand to profit handsomely from further investment? While misplaced optimism could fuel a financial bubble, we have seen in recent months that underestimating the risks posed by AI could also carry other, even existential, costs.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Take Asian Young People’s Jobs?
proj-syn.description: While AI is beginning to affect some entry-level jobs, its effects remain limited and uneven, and there is little evidence of economy-wide displacement. Nonetheless, from updating education and training to strengthening labor-market institutions, policies are needed to support workers amid AI-induced disruption.

proj-syn.title: How Trade Deals Can Save Nature
proj-syn.description: Environmental conservation is among the most important, universally shared imperatives the world faces, and market access is one of the few carrots available in international politics. By linking tariffs to deforestation, the EU and others can create trade agreements that deliver more conservation and more gains from trade.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Third Way on China
proj-syn.description: Instead of choosing between a confrontation with China and business as usual, European policymakers should examine the benefits and costs of trade sector by sector to identify where mutually beneficial arrangements remain possible. Economic modeling shows that pragmatism beats more extreme options in most cases.

proj-syn.title: Alarm Bells in the Balkans
proj-syn.description: Recent developments in the Balkans ought to be a wake-up call for Europe, given the potential for nationalist provocations in one country to spill over within the region. Multiple elections coming next month raise the risk of a dangerous descent into political instability.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s 21st-Century Mercantilism
proj-syn.description: Since his return to the White House, Donald Trump has turned his back on the free-market principles that the United States spent decades championing. In doing so, he threatens to dismantle the economic order that helped produce unprecedented growth in global output and trade.

proj-syn.title: The AI Productivity Delusion
proj-syn.description: As with previous technological revolutions, it is natural to focus on AI's net effects: Will it create more than it destroys? But unlike previous eras of creative destruction, the real question this time is, “Create more of what?”

proj-syn.title: Technological Leapfrogging in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Across Africa, past success stories have led policymakers to believe that developing economies can usually bypass the arduous, expensive stages of infrastructure development by adopting technologies built elsewhere. But this approach deserves more scrutiny, especially when applied to imported AI systems.
